reason: The frame and mesh seem suited to making a surface that spreads the wheels' load across the drift.
expectation: I expect a traction or load-spreading track, though it may need another material.

alternatives.reason: Sifting gravel might help the crossing, but a framed mesh seems more directly like a track.

effect: The frame and mesh made traction panels, as expected; I still need to prepare the crossing.
reaction: Satisfying to see the obvious construction become panels.
reason: Sieving the firm gravel is the only available combination and may prepare material for the crossing.
expectation: I expect sorted gravel, though I am unsure how it will be used with the panels.

effect: Sieving produced coarse route gravel, and the menu now suggests combining it with the panels.
reaction: I am curious how the gravel and panels work together over a soft drift.
reason: The only combination joins the route gravel and panels to prepare the crossing.
expectation: I expect gravel-filled or reinforced traction panels for the rover.

effect: The gravel filled the tracks and completed the preparation; the chapter ends before the crossing or sampling.
reaction: The tracks are a satisfying tangible result, although I wanted to see them used.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the gravel-filled tracks gave a concrete result from the frame, mesh and sorted gravel, tied to the soft crossing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sieving produced gravel without explaining why that grade helps, so the action felt more procedural than informative.

surprise.text: I expected the crossing or coring to follow, so ending with the prepared tracks surprised me.

arbitrary.text: The need to put coarse gravel in the panels was suggested by compatibility, but its physical function was not explained.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see whether the tracks work and what the protected seam contains; this chapter alone felt brief.
